comparable_cases.why_comparable: This is the exact same address (1701 Fillmore St), exact same concept (Super Duper Burgers), exact same square footage (2,950 sq ft), exact same zoning district (NCT-FILLMORE), and exact same use (formula retail restaurant conversion of the former Burger King space). Filed June 2023.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This prior CUA for Super Duper Burgers at 1701 Fillmore was cancelled after 16 months without reaching a Commission hearing. The cancellation (October 2024) offers no decision summary explaining why, so the records do not reveal whether the applicant withdrew due to lease issues, project changes, or Planning concerns. Formula retail requires CUA under Section 303.1 in NCT-FILLMORE.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA to add entertainment to an existing restaurant at 1881 Post St (115 m away, NCD-Japantown), denied July 2013 after 13 months. One of only three dated use decisions within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years; the sole denial in the dataset.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: This is the only denial among nearby use decisions on record. It was for adding entertainment to a restaurant, not for the restaurant use itself. The denial confirms that Planning does scrutinize changes that could increase neighborhood impacts (noise, late hours), but the record gives no reason for the denial.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 47 referral for a non-formula retail restaurant at 1700 Fillmore (52 m away, directly across the street, NCT-FILLMORE), approved October 2022 in 7 days. Shows Planning's treatment of existing restaurants on the same block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approving full-bar license for a non-formula restaurant across the street. Planning explicitly noted 'non-formula retail use' as permitted under Section 760, reinforcing that formula retail status is the trigger for CUA in NCT-FILLMORE, not the restaurant use itself.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral for existing non-formula retail restaurant at 1730 Fillmore (51 m away, same block, NCT-FILLMORE), approved June 2023 in 44 days. Immediate neighbor showing Planning's baseline treatment of restaurants on this block.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved beer-and-wine license for a non-formula restaurant next door to the subject site. Planning noted it is 'permitted in conjunction with existing non-formula retail restaurant use' under Section 760, again confirming formula retail is the discretionary trigger, not restaurant use.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral for Roam Artisan Burgers (a burger restaurant like Super Duper) at 1923 Fillmore (252 m away, NCD-Upper Fillmore), approved November 2022 in 15 days. Comparable fast-casual burger concept in the same Fillmore corridor.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Roam Artisan Burgers, a fast-casual burger chain, operates at 1923 Fillmore with Planning approval for beer-and-wine service. The ABC referral was approved in 15 days for a 'full-service restaurant,' showing that burger concepts are accepted uses on the Fillmore corridor. Roam is also a multi-unit chain, though the referral does not label it formula retail, suggesting it may predate formula retai…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Health permit referral for the subject address (1701 Fillmore, NCT-FILLMORE), approved November 2016. Confirms the prior fast-food restaurant use (Burger King) that the 2023 CUA application proposed to replace.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of a 'self-service/fast food restaurant' at 1701 Fillmore in 2016, confirming the space has been in restaurant use. This agency referral (not a use decision) took 40 days and was for Burger King. It establishes the baseline: restaurant-to-restaurant is not a change of use; formula retail conversion is the discretionary question.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC referral for a catering permit at 1865 Post St (115 m away, NCD-Japantown), approved May 2025 in 2 days. Shows rapid approval timelines for agency referrals in the immediate area.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Agency referral for adding catering to an existing restaurant approved in 2 days, demonstrating that non-discretionary restaurant-related permits move quickly when no change of use or formula retail conversion is involved. This is an agency referral, not a use decision.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning Department to discuss the prior cancelled CUA, formula retail review process, and community outreach expectations.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Explain that Super Duper Burgers is a local Bay Area chain seeking to occupy the former Burger King space at 1701 Fillmore for a fast-casual burger restaurant with no alcohol service. Ask what led to the cancellation of the prior application (2023-004973CUA) and what concerns or gaps need to be addressed. Request guidance on the community outreach plan, public notice timeline, and whether any neighborhood groups or merchants associations should be contacted before filing.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), and file a Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement with the County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The fee is tiered by gross receipts (e.g. $55 for under $100k, $95 for $100k–$250k, plus a $4 state fee). The BAN is issued within 1–5 days and is required for every other city permit and license. If operating as 'Super Duper Burgers' under an entity with a different legal name, file the Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk ($60–120), then publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days.

timeline_cost.notes: This is a timeline and cost range for the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted: Conditional Use Authorization and Health permit to operate. The CUA in NCT-FILLMORE typically takes 120–300 days from filing to Planning Commission approval, including pre-application meeting, environmental review, 300-foot mailed notice, and hearing scheduling. The comparable formula retail CUAs took 167 days (Pinot's Palette, 2015-007413CUA) and 364 days (Orangetheory Fitness, 2018-009861CUA); the cancelled Super Duper CUA at this address took 517 days before cancellation, but that is not a time to approval. Health permit plan check and issuance after final inspection adds 21–60 days for plan review plus 14–45 days for permit issuance, typically overlapping with CUA review and construction. Total government costs: CUA application fee approximately $3,100 (2025–26 schedule for formula retail), DPH plan check $2,207, health permit application $470, business registration $55–700, and building permit $800–15,000 (varies by construction valuation). This does not include construction costs, architect fees, or the building permit timeline (14–120 days for plan check and inspections). The day range is from CUA filing to Commission approval and health permit issuance; it does not include the 30-day appeal period after CUA approval or the time to complete tenant improvement construction.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: The records show 1701 Fillmore St is in the NCT-FILLMORE zoning district and was previously occupied by Burger King as a restaurant. A Conditional Use Authorization (CUA) for Super Duper Burgers at this exact address was filed in June 2023 but was cancelled in October 2024 after 16 months. The pathway analysis confirms this is not a change of use (restaurant to restaurant), so the zoning answer for a new restaurant use is "not decided by the rules"—meaning whether principally permitted or conditional is unclear from the records. The block is extremely active: 17 food/drink businesses and 12 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, with 55 ABC licenses within 1,000 ft. Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 3 dated use decisions for this business type are on file: 1 approved, 1 approved with conditions, and 1 withdrawn—too few to calculate an approval rate.
data_gaps: The records do not explain why the 2023 Super Duper Burgers CUA at this address was cancelled
No hearing transcripts or commission findings are available for the cancelled 2023 application
The zoning pathway does not definitively state whether a restaurant use is principally permitted or requires conditional use in NCT-FILLMORE
ABC license conditions are not exposed in the records, so alcohol-related restrictions on nearby businesses are unknown
No information about whether the Burger King closure left the space vacant or if another tenant occupied it between then and the 2023 application
